definition: Affable means friendly, warm, and easy to talk to.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word affable. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know affable should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Our affable mail carrier lingers at every gate to chat, and even the crankiest houses on the route wave him over.
Approachable is milder than affable — an approachable manager won't bite if you knock, but an affable one pulls up a chair and has you talking in a minute.
Gushing goes further than affable and overshoots it — a gushing host buries you in compliments until you squirm, while affable warmth keeps the conversation easy.

Warm names general kindness and care — a warm coach, a warm note — without saying anything about how conversation flows. Affable is narrower: friendliness that shows up specifically in easy, welcoming talk. A warm person may be shy and quiet; an affable one has you chatting within a minute.

Personable means pleasing in manner and appearance overall — a good first impression from across the room. Affable pins the pleasantness to conversation itself: easy to approach and easy to talk with. A personable candidate looks and carries herself well; an affable one makes the interview feel like a chat.
